messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In lions, one of the most striking examples of a dominant genetic trait is the development of a mane in adult male individuals. The presence of a mane is governed by a dominant allele at a locus that influences the growth of long, dark hair around the head and neck. While females lack this trait, the dominant allele ensures that any male lion carrying it will express the mane phenotype.
